title: Financial Information Return, Township of North Glengarry
publisher: Ontario Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing
notes: Provincially mandated under section 294(1) of the Municipal Act, standardized across all Ontario municipalities and reported on the same schedules year over year. Filed with the ministry by 31 May for the preceding year, so the most recent year always lags. This is the backbone of the financial domain: the only multi-year, comparable financial series available without transcribing a stack of PDFs. Schedules 10 (revenue), 40 (expenses), 60 (continuity of reserves), 70 (long-term liabilities) and 80 (statistical) carry most of what this dashboard needs. Select North Glengarry and the year from the ministry's by-year-and-municipality index.

title: MIDAS — Municipal Information and Data Analysis System
notes: Free web tool that converts Financial Information Return data for every Ontario municipality into multi-year reports and trends. Faster than transcribing the returns by hand and useful for building the comparator set once the sponsor has chosen one. Figures taken from MIDAS should still cite the underlying return, since MIDAS is a presentation layer over it.

title: Financial Information Return, bulk data by year
notes: The same returns as machine-readable CSV covering every municipality from 2000 onward. This is the route to a five-year series without hand transcription, and the route to comparators once they are chosen.

title: Audited Consolidated Financial Statements 2023, Township of North Glengarry
notes: Detail the Financial Information Return flattens: reserve and reserve fund purposes, tangible capital asset continuity, accumulated surplus composition, segment disclosure by department, and the auditor's notes. Read alongside the return, never instead of it.

title: Audited Consolidated Financial Statements 2022, Township of North Glengarry
notes: Includes accumulated surplus and reserve balances as at 31 December 2022.

title: Audited Consolidated Financial Statements 2021, Township of North Glengarry
notes: Earliest audited statements located online. Statements for 2020 and earlier, and for 2024 onward, are not yet located and should be requested from the Treasurer.

title: Audited Consolidated Financial Statements, remaining years
notes: The years not covered by the three statements located above. Needed to complete the five-year series and to pair against each year's budget for variance. Request from the Director of Finance / Treasurer.

title: 2025 Annual Budget, Township of North Glengarry
notes: Approved operating and capital budgets. States a net change to the tax levy of $295,056 and total debt at the start of 2025 of $9.57 million, of which $6.06 million is funded through water and wastewater rates and $3.5 million is tax-supported. That split is the clearest available statement of how much of the township's debt sits on the levy.

title: 2024 Final Operating and Capital Budgets, Township of North Glengarry
2023 Approved Operating and Capital Budgets, Township of North Glengarry
2022 Operating and Capital Budgets, Township of North Glengarry
Budgets and Reports index, Finance Department
notes: The department's own index of budgets and financial reports, listing years back to 2019. Check here first when a year is missing from the direct links recorded in this library, since the township's file URLs change when the site is reorganised.

title: Annual Tax Rate By-law, Township of North Glengarry
notes: The property taxes page carries tax rate documents and by-laws from 2012 onward, including By-law 07-2025 setting the 2025 rates. Sets the rate for each property class. The township portion, the county portion, and the education portion are distinct — the dashboard must not present the township rate as the ratepayer's total.

title: Fees and Charges By-law, Township of North Glengarry
notes: Sets every user fee the township charges, including building permit fees and planning application fees. User fees are own-source revenue and their trajectory is a council decision distinct from the levy.

title: By-laws index, Township of North Glengarry
notes: Council's enacted by-laws. Certified copies are available from the Deputy Clerk. Not every by-law is posted; assume the online set is incomplete until confirmed.

title: Assessment roll summary by property class
notes: Assessment base by class. MPAC assesses and classifies roughly 5.7 million Ontario properties; the municipality does not assess and cannot change a valuation. Current values reflect a valuation date frozen by the province through several postponed reassessment cycles — record the valuation date beside any assessment figure or the levy arithmetic reads wrong. The returned roll summary for the township is not published openly; request it from the Treasurer, who receives it annually.

title: Asset Management Plan 2022, Township of North Glengarry
notes: Anchor document for the infrastructure domain, required under O. Reg. 588/17, which obliges municipalities to review the plan at least every five years. Carries the asset inventory, replacement values, condition distribution, stated levels of service, and the lifecycle funding analysis from which the renewal gap is computed. Confirm which regulatory phase this edition satisfies and the resolution that adopted it. A 2022 plan means replacement values are in 2022 dollars — do not compare them against current-year spending without indexing both to the same year.

title: Strategic Asset Management Policy, September 2018
notes: The policy O. Reg. 588/17 requires alongside the plan. States that the asset management plan will be updated at least every five years. Sets out how asset management is meant to inform budget decisions, which makes it the standard against which the budget process can be checked.

title: Asset Management Plan technical appendices and supporting engineering reports
publisher: Township of North Glengarry / consulting engineers
notes: Per-asset detail behind the class totals in the plan. Usually a separate file and often not posted. Request directly; this is where a gap concentrated in a small number of assets becomes visible as such.

title: Roads needs study and pavement condition assessment
notes: Condition ratings and the methodology behind them. The township's capital planning process is stated to draw on roads needs studies and bridge condition reports alongside the asset management plan, so the document exists even though it is not posted. Record the assessment date: a condition rating without its date is not a fact about today.

title: Ontario Structure Inspection Manual (OSIM) bridge and culvert inspection reports
publisher: Township of North Glengarry / inspecting engineers
notes: OSIM inspections are required on a two-year cycle for structures with a span of three metres or more. County-owned structures are inspected and reported by SDG, which maintains about 195 bridges county-wide. Label the owner on every structure.

title: Alexandria Drinking Water System annual and summary reports
notes: Required under section 11 of O. Reg. 170/03. The URL recorded is the 2024 report; 2023, 2022 and 2021 editions are also posted. This system supplies both Alexandria and Maxville from a treatment plant adjacent to the Mill Pond in Alexandria. The reports carry treatment and distribution detail, sampling and monitoring results, and any adverse water quality incidents — the primary source for the water figures in the infrastructure domain.

title: Glen Robertson Drinking Water System annual and summary reports
notes: A separate, groundwater-sourced system serving the hamlet of Glen Robertson, categorised by the province as a small municipal residential drinking water system. Reported no non-compliance or adverse water quality events in the period covered, but routine testing has found sodium above the recommended upper limit — a reportable condition that carries a public notification obligation and is worth understanding before it arises in a meeting.

title: Drinking water inspection ratings and Chief Drinking Water Inspector reporting
publisher: Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks
notes: Provincial inspection ratings for each municipal residential drinking water system, published through Ontario's Data Catalogue alongside the Chief Drinking Water Inspector's annual report. The ministry's routine inspection produces an Inspection Rating Record per system. Systems are rated individually and must never be averaged into a township-wide figure.

title: Alexandria Wastewater System annual reports
notes: Effluent quality against the Environmental Compliance Approval limits, plus overflow and bypass reporting. Treatment is by sewage lagoon. The 2022 and 2019 reports are also posted. Reported per plant, not township-wide.

title: Utilities: water and sewage system overview
notes: The public description of the distribution and collection systems, and the index to the drinking water annual reports. Records the physical inventory: the Alexandria distribution system holds about 28.2 km of watermain, a 3,000 cubic metre elevated storage tank, 145 hydrants and roughly 1,500 service connections; Maxville holds about 10.2 km of watermain, a 1,500 cubic metre elevated tank, 82 hydrants and roughly 450 connections.

title: Water and wastewater rate study and capacity analysis
notes: Establishes whether the water and wastewater systems are full-cost recovering including renewal, and what the rate path assumes. The 2025 budget records $6.06 million of debt funded through water and wastewater rates, so a rate study or its equivalent underpins that. Also the likely home of any treatment capacity analysis, which is what actually gates serviced growth.

title: Water and sewage fees information
notes: The rates actually charged. Read against the rate study to see whether the charged rate matches the rate the study said full-cost recovery required.

title: SDG Counties Official Plan (2018), February 2025 consolidation
publisher: United Counties of Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry
notes: The operative official plan for North Glengarry is the county plan, not a local one — this is the single most important structural fact in the planning domain. It sets the growth vision to 2036 and establishes where settlement areas, agricultural protection, and growth allocation sit. The 2018 plan came fully into effect for most of SDG following Ontario Land Tribunal decisions dated 15 February 2022 and 21 June 2022; confirm whether any part remains under appeal as it affects the township.

title: Official Plan index and planning services
publisher: United Counties of Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry
notes: The county's index page for the official plan and its amendments. The June 2021 consolidation including OPA 6 and the superseded 2006 plan are also posted, which is where to look when a decision turns on the policy in force at the time.

title: Comprehensive Zoning By-law 39-2000
notes: Zoning is the township's instrument even where the official plan is the county's. Amendments are township council decisions, appealable to the Ontario Land Tribunal. A comprehensive by-law originally passed in 2000 is old enough that whether it reflects current provincial requirements — particularly on additional residential units — is a checkable and consequential question.

title: Zoning By-law and Official Plan Designation Information Guide
notes: Explains how to find the zoning and official plan designation for a specific property through the SDG Explorer community mapping application. The practical route from an address to what may be built on it.

title: Building, Planning and By-law Enforcement Department
notes: The department that authorises all construction and demolition and administers the Ontario Building Code. Entry point for permit records and planning application procedures.

title: Planning staff reports and decision records
notes: Application-by-application record inside the council and committee packages: type, date received, date decided, recommendation, decision, conditions. Processing timelines have to be built from these by hand — no municipality of this size publishes them as a series. Committee of Adjustment and Public Meeting of Planning packages are posted alongside council packages.

title: SDG Counties development tracker
publisher: United Counties of Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry
notes: The county's own tracker for planning applications it decides — subdivisions, condominiums, official plan amendments, and consents. This is the other half of the planning picture: applications on township land that township council does not decide. The route to the approved-but-unbuilt pipeline.

title: Building permit register and Chief Building Official annual report
notes: Permit counts and declared construction value by type. Construction value is the applicant's declared value for fee purposes and is neither a market nor an assessed value; say so wherever it appears. The Building Code Act requires an annual report on building permit fees, which is the most likely published form.

title: Strategic Plan 2023-2027, Township of North Glengarry
notes: Adopted March 2023 for the current council term. Built on three strategic pillars — GROW, FOSTER and CHAMPION — resting on a stated foundation of human resources, information technology, financial stability and corporate values. Whether each pillar carries a checkable measure is a separate question from whether the pillars are the right ones, and the absence of a measure is itself a finding.

title: Corporate Strategy index
notes: The township's own index for the strategic plan and any progress reporting against it. Check here for whether a periodic progress report exists — its presence or absence is the practical test of whether the plan is operative.

title: Council agendas, minutes, staff reports, and recordings
notes: The connective tissue. Covers regular and special council meetings, Committee of the Whole, Committee of Adjustment, and public planning meetings, with agendas, minutes and recordings. Council meets on the second and fourth Mondays of each month except July, August and December, moving to Tuesday when a holiday falls on the Monday — which is the calendar any study cadence tied to council business should follow. Every decision recorded in the council domain cites the meeting date and the report number. Personal information contained in these packages is excluded from this dashboard.

title: SDG Counties council agendas, minutes, and government records
publisher: United Counties of Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry
notes: County-owned roads, paramedic services, social services, long-term care, the county library, and county planning approvals are decided here, not at the township. SDG Counties Council has twelve members drawn from the six local municipalities; North Glengarry sends two, its mayor and deputy-mayor. A complete picture of what a North Glengarry council member votes on requires both agendas.

title: SDG Counties approved budget
publisher: United Counties of Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry
notes: The county levy appears on the North Glengarry ratepayer's bill but is not set by township council alone. The 2024 approved budget was $86 million, described as a 4.36 percent increase for an average residential property. Apportionment among member municipalities is weighted by assessment. County council has since aimed at a 4.48 percent levy increase for 2026 — confirm the adopted figure against the budget document rather than press reporting.

title: SDG Counties audited financial statements
publisher: United Counties of Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry
notes: The county's own financial position, which matters to a township council member who sits on county council and votes on its budget.

title: SDG Counties Strategic Plan 2023-2026
publisher: United Counties of Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry
notes: The county's stated priorities. Where they align or conflict with the township's Strategic Plan 2023-2027 is worth mapping, since a township member sits at both tables.

title: SDG Counties Transportation Services and county road inventory
publisher: United Counties of Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry
notes: The county administers and maintains roughly 982 km of road and 195 bridges county-wide — about 95 km of urban streets and 887 km of rural roads — and runs an annual capital programme of bridge and road repairs and reconstruction. County roads running through North Glengarry are county assets on the county's timetable. Residents do not distinguish them from township roads; the dashboard must. Obtain the split of those kilometres and structures that fall inside the township.

title: Cornwall SDG Paramedic Services reporting and response time standard
publisher: United Counties of Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry
notes: Land ambulance is an upper-tier responsibility. Cornwall SDG Paramedic Services provides 24-hour coverage to a population of over 111,000 across the county and the City of Cornwall. Council-approved response time standards are published annually under provincial regulation, county-wide rather than by municipality. Do not attribute a county-wide figure to North Glengarry; ask the county whether a township-level split is obtainable.

title: SDG social services, housing, and child care service manager reports
publisher: United Counties of Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry
notes: The county is the consolidated municipal service manager. Social housing waitlists and child care capacity are county-reported and cover all member municipalities; a township-level split may not exist.

title: Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry County Library
publisher: United Counties of Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry
notes: Library service in North Glengarry is delivered by the county library system, established in 1971 from the merger of seven existing rural libraries — not by a township library board. This is a tier correction worth carrying: library figures are county figures, and branch-level statistics for the North Glengarry branches must be requested rather than assumed.

title: Ontario public library statistics
publisher: Government of Ontario / Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Sport
notes: Self-reported annual data from every Ontario public library on a standardized basis: circulation, membership, holdings, programming, and finances. Multi-year and comparable, which makes it more useful for trend than any single annual report. Reported for the county library system as a whole.

title: Fire Department service description
notes: The service is a volunteer department of over fifty firefighters across three stations — Alexandria, Apple Hill and Maxville — delivering fire suppression, inspection and education, and medical response support. Three stations across a township of 643 square kilometres is the fact that shapes every response figure in the public safety domain.

title: Fire department annual report and incident statistics
notes: Incident counts by type, roster, apparatus, and training. Not located online; likely presented to council as a staff report rather than published separately. Confirm whether response time is reported and, if so, measured from what event to what event.

title: Fire master plan and community risk assessment
notes: O. Reg. 378/18 requires a community risk assessment to be completed and reviewed on a fixed cycle and used in determining the services the municipality provides. It states the service model and the depth of response council has chosen, which is the only fair benchmark for the service's performance — a national standard designed for career departments would measure the staffing model rather than the service.

title: Ontario Fire Marshal incident and fire loss statistics
publisher: Office of the Fire Marshal, Ontario
notes: Standardized incident reporting across Ontario. Published with a lag, and small-municipality cells may be suppressed for privacy.

title: OPP municipal policing annual billing statement and detachment reporting
publisher: Ontario Provincial Police / Township of North Glengarry
notes: Policing is delivered by the OPP under the provincial billing model: a base cost per property plus a calls-for-service component, both calculated provincially. Governance runs through the Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry OPP Detachment Board. Costs across SDG rose sharply for 2025 — the annual billing statement was reported as up 13.19 percent on the budgeted 2024 amount, and about 20.40 percent once a year-end adjustment was applied, an additional $2,036,153, bringing expected county-wide costs to roughly $11.3 million. Those are county-wide figures and must not be attributed to North Glengarry; obtain the township's own billing statement from the Treasurer.

title: Emergency response plan and annual compliance filing
notes: The Emergency Management and Civil Protection Act requires an adopted plan, an annual exercise, annual training, and a designated emergency information officer. Compliance is filed with the province, so currency is checkable and binary: each requirement is either current or it is not.

title: Census of Population, 2021 — North Glengarry, Township (census subdivision)
notes: Geographic identifier 2021A00053501050, census subdivision code 3501050. The census subdivision boundary matches the municipal boundary, which makes population, dwelling, and household counts directly usable. Smaller geographies such as dissemination areas do not align with settlement boundaries, and labour force data at fine geography carries wide error. State the geography on every community figure.

title: Focus on Geography Series, 2021 Census — North Glengarry
notes: A shorter, chart-led profile of the same census subdivision. Quicker to read than the full profile table when the question is orientation rather than a specific figure.

title: Census Profile, 2016 Census — North Glengarry, Township
notes: The prior cycle, at the same census subdivision code. Definitions change between cycles; note any break in series rather than smoothing it.

title: Focus on Geography Series, 2011 Census — North Glengarry
notes: Records a 2011 population of 10,251 and a change of -3.6 percent from 2006. Needed for multi-census trend. The 2006 figure should be read directly from this profile rather than back-calculated from the percentage.

title: Census Profile, 2021 — Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry, United Counties (census division)
notes: The county geography. The right denominator for anything the county delivers — paramedics, social services, the library — and the wrong one for anything the township delivers.

title: Census of Agriculture — North Glengarry
notes: Farm counts, farm area, farm type, and operator age. Agriculture is the dominant land use across the township's 643 square kilometres and this is the only consistent series on it. Reported at census consolidated subdivision level — confirm that geography's alignment with the municipal boundary before quoting any figure.

title: SDG Counties local statistics and information centre
publisher: United Counties of Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry
notes: The county's own compilation of demographic and economic statistics for its member municipalities. Useful as a cross-check on census figures and as a source for economic indicators the census does not carry — but it is a secondary compilation, so trace any figure back to its origin before relying on it.

title: Ontario Municipal Partnership Fund allocations and technical guide
notes: OMPF is unconditional operating support to 389 municipal governments on an equalization basis, announced annually with a per-municipality workbook showing how the allocation was calculated. The fund rose by $50 million to $600 million for 2026. Because the allocation is formula-driven, its trajectory is knowable in advance of the budget and can be planned against rather than reacted to.

title: Ontario Community Infrastructure Fund and Canada Community-Building Fund allocations
publisher: Government of Ontario / Government of Canada
notes: OCIF provides formula and application-based capital funding for renewal of core infrastructure in small and rural municipalities; the province added $1 billion over five years from 2022. The Canada Community-Building Fund allocation is formula-driven and accumulates in an obligatory reserve fund until spent. Both are eligible for renewal work and are the most direct external lever on the renewal funding gap.

title: Development charges background study and by-law
notes: No development charges by-law has been located for the township, and the fees and charges by-law appears to be the operative instrument for municipal charges. Many rural Ontario townships have no development charges by-law at all, which means growth-related infrastructure is funded from the general levy by all ratepayers rather than by the growth that requires it. Confirm this directly — the absence is a finding, not a gap, and it changes how every development decision should be read.

title: Ontario Land Tribunal decisions and case search
notes: Appeal history for planning decisions, searchable by municipality. The tribunal's decisions of 15 February 2022 and 21 June 2022 are what brought the SDG Official Plan (2018) fully into effect for most of the counties, so the tribunal's record is not merely an appeal log here — it is part of how the operative planning framework came to be.

title: Raisin Region Conservation Authority
notes: One of 36 Ontario conservation authorities, with five member municipalities: North Glengarry, South Glengarry, North Stormont, South Stormont, and the City of Cornwall. Regulated areas constrain development independently of township zoning and conservation authority permission is not a municipal decision. Authority boundaries follow watersheds rather than municipal lines, so confirm whether any part of the township falls under a different authority.

title: Financial Information Returns for comparator municipalities
publisher: Ontario Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing
notes: The comparator set has not been chosen — see the open question on which municipalities the sponsor considers fair. The five other lower-tier municipalities within SDG are the most obviously defensible starting point since they share an upper tier, a county levy, and a planning framework. Wider candidates would be lower-tier Eastern Ontario townships of similar population, assessment base, and road kilometres. Any comparison is context, not judgement.

title: Municipal Study (BMA) financial indicators, if the township participates
notes: Comparator context across Ontario municipalities on a consistent basis. Participation is voluntary and the report is licensed; confirm whether the township or the county subscribes before relying on it.

title: Recreation and facilities reports: registrations, facility usage, rental revenue
notes: Rarely published as a series. Likely to require manual entry from budget presentations and individual staff reports to council. The departmental index is the entry point; the figures themselves sit inside council packages.
